title: An ideal of an Artinian ring has a filtration with length-one quotients
statement: Let $B$ be an Artinian ring (a commutative ring in which every descending chain of ideals is eventually constant) and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$ and ideals $0=J_0\subseteq J_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J_r=J$ of $B$ such that for each $1\le i\le r$ the $B$-module $J_i/J_{i-1}$ has length $1$, i.e. it is nonzero and its only $B$-submodules are $0$ and itself.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian, line 38950): 'As B'_N is Artinian such a filtration exists'; from Lemma Tag 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length, line 12787: an Artinian ring has finite length over itself), Definition Tag 02LY (definition-length) and Lemma Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces, line 12546: a maximal chain of submodules of a finite length module has simple successive quotients)

proof.text: Regard $B$ as a module over itself. The Artinian-ring finite-length lemma [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ring-self-finite-length] gives a finite bound on strict chains of $B$-submodules of $B$.

The ideal $J$ is a $B$-submodule of $B$, so every strict chain of $B$-submodules in $J$ is a strict chain in $B$; hence $J$ has finite length. Apply the simple-filtration lemma [lem-weil-pbc-finite-length-module-simple-filtration] to $M=J$ to obtain $0=J_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq J_r=J$ with each quotient nonzero and without a proper nonzero $B$-submodule. The $B$-submodules of the ideal $J$ are exactly the ideals of $B$ contained in $J$, and the quotient modules are the same, so this is the required ideal filtration. If $J=0$, take $r=0$.
